I was studying the satellite maps last night and I came accross this https://imgtc.ws/POieevW It's 2 big pools with a set of rapids about 1.5kms long in between. The rapids hold massive amounts of brook trout, and we even caught a couple walleye in the pools.

This is a hot spot, not only is it loaded with brookies and walleye, but during the fall and spring the salmon would run through here, there's likely sturgeon and channel catsfish as well as monster pike and musky. Today we just fished the rapids for trout but the bottom pool is definitely canoeable, it's like a small lake. we only made it halfway up the rapids today and caught about a dozen brookies on the way up.

There's old trails for acess, the walk in is about 2 miles, but there are clearings for campsites, its actually an old forgotten place with lots of history, it used to hold a ww2 POW camp where the german prisoners were made to work as loggers, apparently they enjoyed canada and the work a lot and many of them relocated here after the war to work as loggers. There's not much left to show for those days other then some old rotting log piles and the old worn out trails.

Nobody has been in there this year, and I suspect it's not visited at all if ever. The main road is likely still used as a hunting road in the fall but the walking trail is shows no signs of anything except moose.

I'll be spending a lot of time here this summer and I'm sure I'm going to pull out some amazing fish.
